content:
**The five longest‑reigning monarchs (by length of reign) and the names of their fathers**

| Rank | Monarch (Country) | Length of reign | Father (full name & title) |
|------|-------------------|----------------|----------------------------|
| 1 | **Louis XIV** – King of France (1643‑1715) | 72 years 110 days | **Louis XIII**, King of France |
| 2 | **Johann II** – Prince of Liechtenstein (1858‑1929) | 71 years 145 days | **Johann I Joseph**, Prince of Liechtenstein |
| 3 | **Elizabeth II** – Queen of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth (1952‑2022) | 70 years 214 days | **George VI**, King of the United Kingdom |
| 4 | **Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama IX)** – King of Thailand (1946‑2016) | 70 years 126 days | **Mahidol Adulyadej**, Prince of Songkhla (later known as Prince Mahidol of Thailand) |
| 5 | **Hirohito (Emperor Shōwa)** – Emperor of Japan (1926‑1989) | 62 years 13 days | **Emperor Taishō** (personal name **Yoshihito**) |

### Quick notes

* **Louis XIV** (the “Sun King”) inherited the throne at age 4 after the death of his father, Louis XIII.  
* **Johann II** became sovereign at age 23 when his father, Johann I Joseph, died. He ruled Liechtenstein for more than seven decades.  
* **Elizabeth II** ascended the throne at age 25 following the death of her father, George VI.  
* **Bhumibol Adulyadej** succeeded his older brother, King Ananda Mahidol (Rama VIII), and his father, Prince Mahidol, had been a prominent medical doctor and member of the Thai royal family.  
* **Emperor Hirohito** became Japan’s emperor at age 25 after the death of his father, Emperor Taishō.  

These five reigns remain the longest in recorded monarchical history (as of 2025).
